newsitem.title: USA: Applied Extrusion ends acquisition talks.
newsitem.headline: Applied Extrusion ends acquisition talks.

text.p: Applied Extrusion Technologies Inc said Friday it would terminate acquisition talks with an unnamed company for an international oriented polypropylene films manufacturing business because the parties failed to reach mutually agreeable terms.

The company said in a press release it expects to take an $0.08 per share, $900,000 after-tax third-quarter charge for "extensive due diligence efforts and other expenditures related to the proposed transaction.

"We continually explore and evaluate prospects for strategic acquisitions, and have positioned AET to be a consolidator in the specialty films industry," said chief executive Thomas Williams. "While we are disappointed with the outcome in this instance, we are committed to global expansion and will continue to use a disciplined approach to evaluate potential business combinations with the ultimate goal of enhancing shareholder value."
The company said the negotiations were confidential.
Applied Extrusion Technologies develops and manufactures specialized plastic films used primarily in consumer product labeling, flexible packaging and health care applications.
